ai.title: Deprecate peak surcharge in FreebuffFreebucksInfo
ai.summary: The `peak` field in `FreebuffFreebucksInfo` is marked deprecated. New servers omit this field because Flash now uses Luminal's flat rate. The change resides in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`. The field remains for backward compatibility with older server responses.

eli5.text: When you check your usage credits, the system no longer shows a special "peak" price surcharge badge for Flash models, because Flash now uses a flat rate instead. If you were using an older server or app that still expects that peak badge, it will simply leave the field blank rather than breaking. This only affects how the credit details are displayed behind the scenes; your actual usage and billing are unchanged.

entries.title: SDK update: byok

ai.title: SDK run() allows inference source change when opted
ai.summary: The SDK's `run()` function now accepts an `allowInferenceSourceChange` option in `RunOptions`; when set, it permits resuming a conversation on a different inference source (such as moving from hosted inference to a user-selected BYOK connection) that the default source-pinning guard would otherwise refuse, with the comment specifying that hosts must only enable this for a user-selected connection and never as an error fallback. The guard condition in `run.ts` now checks `!options.allowInferenceSourceChange` before rejecting source or BYOK connection mismatches, while `sdk/src/client.ts` documents that `run()` enforces the history pin unless the host explicitly authorizes a switch. In `sdk/src/byok.ts`, the `lookup()` error messages were reworded to 'select another provider or a Freebuff model to continue' and 'select its current revision to continue'.
ai.evidence: sdk/src/run.ts adds RunOptions field `allowInferenceSourceChange?: boolean` (with a doc comment stating hosts must only enable it for a user-selected connection), and the run() body gates the hosted-to-BYOK / BYOK-mismatch refusal on `!options.allowInferenceSourceChange`; sdk/src/byok.ts lookup() error strings change from 'choose a connection for a new task'/'start a new task with its current revision' to 'select another provider or a Freebuff model to continue'/'select its current revision to continue', and sdk/src/client.ts updates an inline comment to 'run() enforces the history pin unless the host explicitly authorizes a switch.'
ai.migration: No migration is required; existing hosts that do not set `allowInferenceSourceChange` retain the prior refusal behavior, while hosts that wish to resume a BYOK connection session from a hosted run or switch sources on resume must now pass `allowInferenceSourceChange: true`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer of `allowInferenceSourceChange` beyond the `RunOptions` type and the guard condition in `run()`.

ai.title: Freebucks reset and timezone modules added to CLI and shared types
ai.summary: Two new shared modules define Freebucks reset policy copy and timezone header logic: `common/src/util/freebucks-reset.ts` exports `FREEBUCKS_RESET_POLICY_COPY`, `FREEBUCKS_REFILL_PENDING_LABEL`, `freebucksRefillPending`, and `freebucksResetCopy`, while `common/src/util/freebucks-timezone.ts` exports `FREEBUCKS_TIMEZONE_HEADER`, `normalizeFreebucksTimeZone`, and `freebucksTimeZoneHeaders`. The CLI now sends the `x-fb-timezone` header on every session request and shows `Updating balance…` when the daily pool deadline has passed, replacing the previous hardcoded Pacific-time reset copy with the shared policy string. The wire type `FreebuffFreebucksWindow` gains an optional `resetTimeZone` field so the displayed reset time reflects the account's scheduled timezone rather than Pacific time.
ai.evidence: Commit [990e9235] adds two new modules `common/src/util/freebucks-reset.ts` and `common/src/util/freebucks-timezone.ts`; `cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts` imports `FREEBUCKS_REFILL_PENDING_LABEL`, `FREEBUCKS_RESET_POLICY_COPY`, and `freebucksRefillPending` from the reset module and replaces the hardcoded Pacific reset text in `FREEBUCKS_PICKER_NOTICE` with `${FREEBUCKS_RESET_POLICY_COPY}`; `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts` imports and spreads `freebucksTimeZoneHeaders()` into every session request; `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` adds `resetTimeZone?: string` to `FreebuffFreebucksWindow`, updates the `poolDate`/`poolLocalDate` docblocks on `FreebuffDesktopRefundInfo`, and clarifies the `FreebuffFreebucksWindow` docblock.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show consumers of `freebucksResetCopy` or `normalizeFreebucksTimeZone` reading the new `resetTimeZone` value, nor a server-side reader for the `x-fb-timezone` header, so the end-to-end rollout of timezone-aware resets is not visible here.

ai.title: Sponsored v2 capability inspection and local-execution containment
ai.summary: The CLI now inspects a project's sponsored-run capability before polling ads: `sponsored-project-identity.ts` writes a UUID marker to `.freebuff/project-id` at project selection, `sponsored-cli-capability.ts` gathers framework, package manager, git, and containment facts, and `useGravityAd` sends `sponsoredCapability`/`capabilityInspection` to `/api/ads` on `FREEBUFF_WEB_URL` when a capable project is detected. The change spans the CLI ad rail, the common capability schema, and the SDK sandbox probe.

ai.title: Add first-tab discount offer to Freebucks pricing
ai.summary: Freebuff introduces an account-wide first-tab discount that opts a session into a per-user Freebucks reduction on a single session at a time, shared across Desktop and CLI. The CLI polls `firstTabQuoteForSession` against the live owning session so that switching the owner releases its discount before the next purchase while other tabs and detached purchases keep the account quote. A new `first_tab_discount_changed` admission status and the `x-freebuff-first-tab-discount` request header carry the choice onto the POST that admits a session, and the model selector now renders a 'First-tab discount' detail chip plus a copy block when the offer is active.
ai.evidence: New files `common/src/util/freebuff-first-tab-discount.ts` and `common/src/util/freebuff-price-selection.ts` introduce first-tab discount constants and selection class. `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts` adds `FIRST_TAB_DISCOUNT_HEADER` import and a `firstTabDiscount` option on `callFreebuffSession`. `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` adds `firstTabDiscount` field to `FreebuffFreebucksInfo` and a `first_tab_discount_changed` admission status member. `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx` imports `firstTabDiscountCopy` and renders a 'First-tab discount' detail chip when available.

ai.title: Add sponsored delivery client diagnostics reporter
ai.summary: A new reporter `sponsoredDeliveryClientDiagnostics` in `common/src/ads/sponsored-delivery-diagnostics.ts` normalizes client claims - user-agent, reported OS, and capability inspection state - into a diagnostic payload whose fields (`client_os`, `execution_surface`, `capability_contract`, `capability_inspection`) mirror the inputs rather than overriding them. The function infers `execution_surface` as `desktop_${os}` or `cli_${os}` only when a surface product and a known OS are both present, and classifies the capability contract as `v2`, `v2_inspection_only`, `v1`, or `not_reported` based strictly on which inspection objects exist. Tests confirm it does not translate Windows requests into Mac ones, separates legacy evidence from missing reports, and keeps free-text OS values out of telemetry.
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/ads/sponsored-delivery-diagnostics.ts` adds the exported function `sponsoredDeliveryClientDiagnostics`, which derives `client_os`, `execution_surface`, `capability_contract`, and `capability_inspection` from `userAgent`, `reportedOs`, `sponsoredCapability`, `capabilityInspection`, and `hasLegacyCapability` inputs. The accompanying tests assert only that client claims are reported and that legacy capability state does not mutate the inferred OS.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer or telemetry pipeline reads the returned diagnostic object, nor whether this is intended to precede a downstream authorization gate.
